Definition: probably ultimately from the base of G3433 (through the idea of hardship); a "mill", i.e. (by implication), a grinder (millstone):--millstone.
BiblicalUsage: Mylos is a millstone — whoever offends one of these little ones, it were better a millstone were hanged about his neck and he were drowned in the depth of the sea, and two women shall be grinding at the mill when one is taken.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the millstone is the measure of the sin: what is done to the little ones is weighed, and the weight is terrible.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
